clue.text: Chap, stony broke, Austen's Mr Collins?

indicators.note: broke suggests something smashed apart, so these letters are pieced together in a new order

explanation.surface: A penniless fellow is likened to the fawning clergyman in Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like it describes the chap's finances, but it tells you to rearrange CHAPSTONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Collins in Pride and Prejudice is the classic fawning flatterer, so the question mark marks him as an example of a toady.

clue.text: Cheat succeeded and was cocky

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
crew is an old past tense of crow, what a cock does

explanation.surface: A swindler prospered and swaggered about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was cocky' looks like boasting, but it means behaved as a cockerel, which crows; CREW is the old past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw someone is slang for to swindle or cheat them.

clue.text: Make remark about role, one of many coach may have

definitions.text: one of many coach may have

indicators.note: about says the remark's letters surround the role

parts.note: to comment is to make a remark
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone comments on a role that a drama coach might assign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a trainer, but it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway coach is divided into several compartments, separate sections with seats.

clue.text: Soft toy shaken by kid is rabbit

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a rattle is a noisy toy that babies shake

explanation.surface: A soft cuddly toy, rattled by a child, turns out to be a bunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' looks like the toy, but it is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to rabbit on is to talk at length about trivia, the same as to babble.

clue.text: Outside broadcasts of Leopardstown's first races

indicators.note: broadcasts suggests things scattered widely, so these letters are strewn and reassembled
first takes only the opening letter of the racecourse's name

explanation.surface: TV crews cover the opening races at an Irish racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopardstown is a racecourse near Dublin. 'broadcasts' scrambles OF, L and RACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, from Italian, means in the open air, so outdoors.

clue.text: Hypothesis does, possibly, stand up in your case

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: thy is the old form of your, here acting as a casing

indicators.note: stand up, in a down clue, lifts the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a roe is a kind of deer, and does are female deer

explanation.surface: A theory might hold up in your particular situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like the verb but is the plural of doe, a female deer; 'stand up' turns the deer upward to EOR, and 'in your case' means held inside the old word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, a supposition still to be proved.

clue.text: High-quality pupils?

definitions.meaning: top-notch, first-rate, as in a player with real style
a group of schoolchildren taught together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both excellence, as in a player of real quality, and a set of pupils taught together in school.

clue.text: Reckon old politician's outwardly clever

indicators.note: outwardly says the clever word goes on the outside

parts.note: cute can mean shrewd or clever
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: Someone judges a former MP to be superficially smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' looks like it qualifies clever in the surface, but it says the clever word encloses the former politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To compute is to calculate, to reckon a figure.

clue.text: Fool of a girl losing her head

indicators.note: the girl loses her first letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A silly girl loses her head.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Turning to the left, wrong trail's somehow followed

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the wrong, so they come second

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone takes a left turn and follows the wrong path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' reorders the trail's letters into ISTRAL; the possessive's S counts here as a letter, and 'followed' places it after the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinistral means left-handed or spiralling to the left, from Latin sinister, left.

clue.text: Drink sailor knocked back after dance

parts.note: rum is a spirit drunk by sailors

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the sailor's letters run in reverse

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor downs his drink after an evening of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like the sailor downing his drink, but it reverses the able seaman to give BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: His order's a secret one to rescue close family members

parts.note: to free someone is to rescue them
a mother, MA, and a son are both close relatives
a mother, MA, and a son are both close relatives

explanation.surface: A man belongs to a secretive brotherhood pledged to save his kin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: the man described belongs to an order famous for its secret rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasonry is a fraternal order known for secret rituals and handshakes, so its member belongs to a secret order.

clue.text: Treasurer who set out to be dominant in union

indicators.note: out signals letters set loose and put back in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A treasurer sets out to dominate a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it means marriage; 'out' shuffles TREASURERWHOSET.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the partner who takes charge in a marriage, the one who makes the decisions at home.

clue.text: Return home of one who offended old custom

definitions.text: Return home of one who offended

parts.note: ex means former or old
a tradition is a long-established custom

explanation.surface: An offender is sent back home under an ancient custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Extradition is the handing over of an accused person to the country where the crime was committed.

clue.text: An operetta, in more than one case, sounding like this

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken the same way as the plural of the medical cases

parts.note: cases in a hospital are the people being treated, so several cases are patients

explanation.surface: A light opera is described as resembling several cases.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the word for several medical cases sounds exactly like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote a comic operetta of this name satirising aesthetes.

clue.text: Frank goes on to quarrel, accusing person in suit

parts.note: plain means frank or outspoken
a tiff is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: Frank moves on to an argument, blaming a man in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a civil lawsuit against another.

clue.text: Somebody advising soldiers to run

parts.note: soldiers are often called men in crosswords
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An adviser tells soldiers to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is an experienced counsellor who guides a less experienced person.

clue.text: Impetus needed after second pause during speech

indicators.note: the hesitation comes after the time word, so it goes second

parts.note: a moment is a very short time, a second
um is the noise of a hesitating speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker needs a boost after pausing for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the driving force that keeps something moving, the impetus.

clue.text: Guy following a military order

indicators.note: the piece for Guy follows the a, so it comes second

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A man named Guy obeys a military command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning mock.
explanation.definitionFit: The command lets soldiers stand relaxed, feet apart, after standing to attention.

clue.text: Resilient agent eclipsing his colleagues?

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering, so the agent wraps around his colleagues

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a spy's fellows form a spy ring

explanation.surface: A tough secret agent outshines his fellow spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipsing' looks like outshining, but it means covering; the question mark flags that a spy's colleagues form a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back into shape, as a resilient material does.

clue.text: Lay aside in relaxing bath, expecting girl round

indicators.note: round says the girl's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: moll is old slang for a girl, especially a gangster's

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the word bath so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies back in a soothing bath while waiting for a girl to come round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' loosens the bath into THBA, and 'round' wraps the gangster's girl about it; 'expecting' is only a joining word in the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball something is to put it into storage, unused, for possible later revival.

clue.text: Mess man's got into supplying drug

indicators.note: got into says the man's word goes inside the mess

parts.note: a hash is a mess, as in making a hash of something
his is what belongs to a man

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the mess are dealing narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like the army dining hall, but it means a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, a narcotic drug.

clue.text: Sound terrified in riot

definitions.meaning: a hilarious person or thing, as in she was a riot at the party

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a shriek of terror and informal for something or someone hilarious.

clue.text: Keen fan finds fine example, following ballet music

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a golf nut
a cracker is something excellent of its kind
a suite is a retinue of followers

explanation.surface: An enthusiast discovers a superb specimen after watching the ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like an order word, but it is the noun for an entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky drew an orchestral suite from his Christmas ballet score.

clue.text: Dodge coming from South Eastern chap

indicators.note: in a down clue coming from the south means reading upwards

parts.note: Dave stands for any chap

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps a man from the South East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Eastern' looks like one phrase, but 'coming from South' reverses E plus DAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to dodge or escape something.

clue.text: Working together to produce popular performance

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: Musicians collaborate to put on a crowd-pleasing show.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act jointly, in agreement with others.

clue.text: Dog's short docked tail

indicators.note: docked tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt

explanation.surface: A dog has a short, docked tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the tail, but it means CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a mongrel or worthless dog.

clue.text: Resort of extreme characters, ones holding bishop back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read in reverse

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at either end of the alphabet

indicators.note: holding says the ones have the bishop between them

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, so ones is two of them
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A holiday resort is described in terms of extreme characters and a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts B between I and I to give IBI; 'back' reverses AZIBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Balearic island famous as a holiday and clubbing destination.

clue.text: During quarrel love to make sudden attack

indicators.note: During puts the love inside the quarrel

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: In the middle of a lovers' tiff, one launches a surprise assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is the tennis score nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid or incursion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Parent taking risk is struck dumb

parts.note: mum is a British word for mother
to chance something is to risk it; a chance is a risk

explanation.surface: A mother gambling leaves someone speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumchance is an old word for silent or tongue-tied, from a game played in silence.
